objects.description: No custom types are defined in this header. It only declares two C-linkage functions: simplewall_version and simplewall_sum. There are no structs, enums, typedefs, or classes to document.

functions.name: simplewall_version
functions.description: Returns the library's version as a C string. Typical usage: call at any time to retrieve a human-readable version identifier. The pointer refers to read-only memory; ownership/lifetime are not documented in the header and are therefore unknown.
requirements: Do not modify the returned string (it is const).
Do not free or deallocate the returned pointer unless documentation elsewhere explicitly grants ownership (ownership/lifetime are unspecified).
Assume it returns a pointer to a null-terminated C string; nullability is not specified—callers should defensively handle a potential null return.

functions.name: simplewall_sum
functions.description: Computes and returns the sum of two integers. Intended for straightforward integer addition.
requirements: Arguments a and b may be any values representable by int.
If the implementation performs plain signed integer addition, passing values whose sum overflows int may result in undefined behavior; prefer values whose sum lies within [INT_MIN, INT_MAX].
No pointers or external state are involved; no specific initialization is indicated by the header.
